cases.name: flat
cases.note: SCI-04. Every consecutive step is 0 >= -slack, so the old geometry test said monotone; the ladder carries no dose information at all and Spearman is undefined. Insufficient variation is not monotone.

cases.name: decreasing
cases.note: Direction is OBSERVED, not prespecified: a consistently downward ladder is monotone here (rho = -1). See the direction contract in both docstrings.

cases.name: inverted
cases.note: Rises then collapses: a real step violation, rho = -0.5 and defined.

cases.name: two-points-unequal
cases.note: Two points are enough when they differ.

cases.name: single-point
cases.note: Fewer than two points is never monotone; rho needs two.

cases.name: repeated-doses
cases.note: PINS the PARTIAL-tie behaviour (at least two distinct doses), deliberately unchanged: pairs sort by (alpha, effect), so the two rows at alpha 1.0 are ordered 0.1 then 0.3 and the repeat never manufactures a step violation. Spearman gives the tied doses their average rank, so rho is 0.866..., not 1.

cases.name: all-doses-tied
cases.note: Zero DOSE range (owner's ruling, 2026-09-05): every alpha is the same, so the (alpha, effect) tie-break sorted the effects by themselves and the rising 'ladder' the step check used to pass was manufactured by the sort. Mirror of 'flat' — zero variation on the dose axis instead of the effect axis — and rho is undefined for the same zero-rank-variance reason. Both engines answer (NaN, false). Partial ties ('repeated-doses') are unchanged.

cases.name: nonfinite-effect
cases.note: A NaN effect is refused BEFORE the sort: comparing NaN is not a strict weak ordering, and a NaN comparison is false, which could otherwise smuggle a true verdict out.

cases.name: nonfinite-alpha
cases.note: Same refusal on the dose side.

cases.name: tolerance-just-inside
cases.note: Range 0.5, so slack = 0.05 * 0.5 = 0.025; the single backward step is -0.02 and is forgiven.

cases.name: tolerance-just-outside
cases.note: Same ladder, slack = 0.03 * 0.5 = 0.015 < 0.02, so the same step is a violation. The tolerance arithmetic is unchanged by SCI-04.

cases.name: tiny-but-nonzero-increase
cases.note: PINS the edge of the SCI-04 fix: the range is 1e-9, not 0, so this still passes. The fix refuses ZERO variation only — it is not a minimum-effect-size gate, and must not silently become one.

nonfiniteEncoding: JSON has no NaN or Infinity literal and Foundation's JSONSerialization refuses the non-standard tokens, so a nonfinite alpha or effect is written as one of the strings "nan", "inf", "-inf". Both loaders map those strings back to Double values.
note: Cross-engine contract for dose-response monotonicity: Python steerlab_server.experiment.study_stats.dose_monotonicity and Swift StudyStatistics.doseMonotonicity must return the same verdict for every case here. Unlike most files in this directory, this one is HAND-AUTHORED and is not produced by scripts/regenerate-cross-engine-fixtures.py: it states the INTENDED contract (external review, 2026-09-05, SCI-04) rather than dumping one engine's current output, so both engines are measured against it rather than against each other's drift. Unequal-length inputs are deliberately absent — the two engines answer differently there by design (Python raises, Swift returns a NaN refusal) and each suite pins its own behaviour.
